raw_response:
Well, let me think about this year's plan. I've been doing this for 45 years now, so I know my fields pretty well. My nine mu is split — about 5 mu I put in cotton on the sandier part near the south end, and the other 4 mu I'll plant to spring maize on the better ground. That's how I've done it the last few years and it works. My husband helps some but he's also doing a little work in town, and my son is mostly off-farm now, so I really only have my own two hands most days. That's why I can't handle too much land or too complicated a setup.

**For the cotton (5 mu):**
I'll plant around April 20th, maybe a few days earlier if the soil warms up. I buy the transgenic seed from the supply store — the regular bollworm-resistant kind, costs about 60 yuan per mu for seed. I don't save my own seed anymore, the hybrids don't come true. Before planting I'll put down a compound fertilizer as base — maybe one bag of 15-15-15 for every two mu, so about 25 kg per mu of compound. That gives me roughly 3-4 kg N, some P and K. Then I'll topdress urea at squaring (around late June) — about 10-12 kg urea per mu, which is another 4-5 kg of N. So total N maybe 8-9 kg per mu. I know the extension guy says you can push it to 15 or more, but cotton on my sandy field doesn't pay back more fertilizer, and I've seen my neighbor waste money putting extra on. 

Water — I'll irrigate once before planting to get the seedbed moist, then maybe once at squaring if it's dry, and once at boll-fill. Three times is what I usually do. Pumping from the well isn't cheap, the electric meter runs fast. 

Pesticide — yes, I have to spray. Even with the Bt cotton I still get aphids and mirid bugs. I'll spray maybe 3-4 times across the season. And I have to hand-weed or use one herbicide application early. 

Yield I'm hoping for around 250 kg of lint per mu. Last year I got 240. If the weather is decent I might hit 270.

**For the spring maize (4 mu):**
Plant around April 25th — spring maize goes in early, before the ground gets too warm. I use Zhengdan 958 or whichever hybrid the village store has good stock of — around 40 yuan/mu for seed. Before planting I put down compound fertilizer, about 30 kg/mu of 15-15-15 as base, and then I topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (around early July) — maybe 15 kg urea per mu. So total N is around 11-12 kg/mu. Spring maize can yield well, my neighbor who does everything a bit more intensive gets 550 kg/mu, but I'm honestly happy with 450-480.

Irrigation — spring maize really needs water because it's growing through the hot dry part of the summer. I'll irrigate at planting, at jointing, at tasseling, and once during grain fill if needed. Three times minimum, four if it's a dry year.

Tillage — I hire the rotary tiller man in the village, costs about 50 yuan/mu, one pass before planting. I don't own the machine. For cotton I'll also have him run the planter.

Labor is the tightest thing. I do most of the work myself, my husband helps when he's around. Maybe I'll hire someone for a few days at cotton picking time — that's the killer, picking takes so many hours.
